writeup.headline: Thermo Fisher rates Hold: strong momentum and solid quality offset by high valuation and a leveraged balance sheet.
writeup.thesis: Thermo Fisher scores 56, a Hold, because strong share-price trend and good business quality are balanced by weak balance-sheet and valuation scores. The trend factor scores 93, with the price at its 52-week high, 27.9% above its 200-day average, and shares 42.2 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Quality scores 74 on a 17.6% operating margin, a 15.8% FCF margin, low stock-based pay and diluted share count down 1.9% year on year. Growth is moderate at 57: TTM revenue growth of 7.2%, latest-quarter revenue growth of 10.5% year on year, and growth sped up by 4.3 pp from the previous quarter. Holding the score back, valuation scores 24, with a P/FCF of 35.6x and an EV/EBIT of 36.7x, both high in absolute terms, and multiples that are expensive against its own history. The balance sheet scores 19, with net debt at 5.22 times FCF and cash covering only 0.1 of debt.
key_risks: Valuation is high in absolute terms, with FCF yield 2.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and EV/EBIT is more expensive than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends.
Leverage is meaningful: net debt is 5.22 times FCF and cash to debt is 0.1.
Part of the Q3 beat came from a one-time tariff refund, so the underlying improvement may be smaller than the headline suggests.
Specialty Diagnostics declines and a biotech reagent market that has not yet recovered weigh on parts of the business.
After a sharp run to its 52-week high, the shares are exposed to a pullback if results or guidance disappoint.
what_would_change: An upgrade to Buy needs 9 more points, for example from sustained revenue acceleration lifting the growth score or a cheaper valuation after a price pullback.
Reducing net debt relative to FCF would lift the weak balance-sheet score and support a higher rating.
A downgrade to Sell would need a 12-point drop, such as momentum fading from its current highs together with growth slowing back down.
Negative guidance or analyst news replacing the current mildly positive news ratings would also push the score lower.
